limitations: The running retained worker uses the September 11 image digest sha256:39f0361c2c4492158362ce603c6fdaddfad40c99f120afb4760ea0e1ed51bbbf; d228 worker-side durable-receipt changes are not deployed.

The old controller gracefully removed its worker during bootout, so the first guardian start cold-started a same-volume worker. Adoption was proven on subsequent controller crash and pause handovers, not at the initial cutover.
No independent workload recorder was available; duplicate execution remains a contract assertion rather than an independently observed production fact.
Docker-daemon restart, host reboot, delayed startup, storage faults, retained-state restoration and restart-budget exhaustion remain isolated ACT-018 drills.

rollback.before_admission: bootout new guardian, prove process group/listener gone, restore old plist and let old owner create its marker
rollback.after_admission_or_unknown: do not start old binary; preserve new journals/tombstones, keep admissions blocked and reconcile or use a compatible rollback binary

acceptance: partial: host guardian/controller recovery and worker restart-policy cutover are deployed and canaried; ACT-019 remains open for the retained worker image boundary and state-compatible post-admission rollback.
